LIVE_MEASURED.label: Live measured
LIVE_MEASURED.help: Measured on this machine during this session, by the code shown in the Code Explorer.

VERIFIED_IMPORTED.label: Verified import
VERIFIED_IMPORTED.help: Imported from a file whose schema and checksum were verified. Measured elsewhere, not on this machine.

DEMO_SAMPLE.label: Demo sample
DEMO_SAMPLE.help: Synthetic numbers for teaching. Never a measurement and never used as evidence.

NOT_RUN.label: Not run
NOT_RUN.help: This step did not run, usually because the machine lacks a required capability.

FAILED.label: Failed
FAILED.help: The step ran and failed. The failure is kept as a record; nothing is hidden.

approval.title: Approval needed
approval.note: Nothing runs until you approve. You can copy the command and run it yourself instead.
approval.model_download_uses_network_and_disk: Downloading a model uses network bandwidth and disk space.
approval.vllm_uses_gpu_and_pulls_container_image: vLLM uses the GPU and may pull a large container image.
approval.large_benchmark: This benchmark is large and may take a long time.

source.executedHelp: This is the real file the lab runs, read from disk. Not an illustration.
source.modifyBody: The explorer is read-only. Edit the file in your own editor, then run the related tests listed for the step.
source.title: Source code

q.line: What does the selected line do?
q.why: Why is it written this way?
q.change: What happens if I change it?

tutor.placeholder: Ask about this step, the code, or a result…

charts.compareAria: Bar chart comparing baseline and candidate metrics
charts.stripAria: Dot plot of per-request end-to-end latency for each trial
charts.sweepAria: Line chart of TTFT p50 versus concurrency

kv.title: KV cache: reserve everything vs pages
kv.sub: Each row is one request. Cyan is cache actually used; red is memory reserved but wasted. Paged allocation (the PagedAttention idea) hands out small blocks on demand.

lt.title: Latency vs throughput
lt.sub: A server that handles one request at a time makes waiting clients queue. A batching server serves them together.
lt.assumptions: Toy model: 40 ms per request alone; each extra request in a batch adds 15% to the step time. Real servers differ; measure yours in the Arena.

missions.scanFirst: Scan your machine first (Mission 01) so the lab knows which paths are available.
missions.lockNote: A mission unlocks when its prerequisites are verified by checks, not by clicking through.
missions.observeIntro: Observe mode: the lab runs the steps that need no approval and explains each result. Steps that need approval or missing hardware are skipped and shown as such.
missions.missingCaps: Not available on this machine (needs: {{caps}}). It will be recorded as NOT RUN.
missions.runWithoutApproval: Try without approval (it will be blocked)
missions.validationNote: Checks are deterministic rules on the run's real output. The tutor never decides completion.
missions.reproduce: Run it yourself in a terminal

challenge.label: Challenge
challenge.title: Do it without the walkthrough
challenge.noHints: No hints here. The same checks decide whether you did it.

lab.machineIntro: Start here. The scan runs fixed, read-only commands (nvidia-smi, docker version, Python imports) and records what it finds.
lab.noGpuHelp: That's fine: every core mission has a CPU path. GPU steps are marked NOT RUN.
lab.welcomeSub: Run a real model on your own hardware, measure it honestly, read the code that did it, and decide what to change.
lab.skillsSub: Earned from verified steps, not from clicks.
lab.noSkills: No skills yet. Verify a step to earn one.

garage.noEstimate: Not enough metadata to estimate memory.
garage.twoWorkflows: Two workflows: inspect a Hub model by ID or URL (metadata only, nothing downloaded), or inspect a model already on disk.
garage.inspectSub: Paste a Hugging Face model ID or https://huggingface.co/… URL.
garage.modelChanged: Note: showing a new model; the previous one was {{prev}}.
garage.catalogSub: Small models that run on a CPU. The tiny one is built locally and needs no network.
garage.noLocal: No local models yet. Build the tiny model to start.
garage.randomNote: This model has random weights, so the text is gibberish. The timings and tokens are still real.

code.pick: Pick a file on the left, or use View source from a mission step.
code.legendExecuted: real files from this repository; the code that runs.
code.legendIllustrative: simplified snippets in explanations; labelled wherever they appear.
code.legendSuggested: changes proposed by the tutor; never applied automatically.
code.readOnly: Read-only. Secrets, .env files, .git and dependencies are not served.

research.intro: Every record links to a primary source and says how it was checked. If a source could not be verified, it is labelled.
research.pick: Pick a source to read the summary.

arena.serverSub: Start an OpenAI-compatible server bound to 127.0.0.1. The mini server runs on CPU; vLLM needs a GPU and Docker.
arena.benchSub: Closed-loop load: each virtual client sends its next request when the previous one finishes. Warm-up requests are discarded.
arena.hypothesisPh: e.g. TTFT will rise with concurrency because the mini server is serial
arena.benchNote: Needs a healthy server. Results are saved as LIVE MEASURED experiments.
arena.compareSub: A fair comparison changes one variable. The lab checks this for you.
arena.needTwo: Run at least two benchmarks to compare.

warn.non_measured_provenance: One side is not a live or verified measurement.
warn.more_than_one_variable_changed: More than one variable changed, so you cannot tell which one caused the difference.
warn.no_variable_changed: Nothing changed between the two; differences are noise.

arena.suggestNote: Suggestions are rule-based hypotheses. Validate them with another measured run before you rely on them.

sugg.queueing_serial: Requests are queueing behind a serial server

arena.sweepSub: The dashed line is a synthetic teaching example. The solid line is your measured TTFT p50 for the same model and max_tokens.
arena.sweepHint: Run benchmarks at concurrency 1, 2 and 4 to draw your own line.

journal.notesSub: Your words. Notes never change the measured result.
journal.reportSub: Only live or verified measurements are claimed as results. Demo, failed and not-run records are listed separately.
journal.decisionPh: What will you deploy, and why does the evidence support it?
journal.runsSub: Every run, including blocked, not-run and failed ones.
journal.importNote: Imports are checked (schema + checksum) and labelled VERIFIED IMPORTED.
journal.pickExp: Pick an experiment to see its details and notes.
